ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r2.claim: Al-sābighāt are coats of mail; the word first meant full or complete and came to designate armor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r2.anchor: السابغات: الدروع، وأصله الوصف بالسبوغ، وهو التمام والكمال، وغلب على الدروع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r3.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses سوابغ for complete white coats of mail that arrows cannot pierce.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر: عليها أسود ضاريات لبوسهم ... سوابغ بيض لا يخرقها النبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r4.claim: Al-sard is joining one thing to another of the same kind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r4.anchor: السرد: إتباع الشيء بالشيء من جنسه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r5.speaker: الشماخ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r5.claim: Al-Shammākh’s verse uses sard for a repeated, linked sequence, comparing it to sheep being threaded together.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p512#3/r5.anchor: قال الشماخ: فظن تباعا خيلنا في بيوتكم ... كما تابعت سرد الضأن الخوارز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r1.claim: A coat is called masrūda because its rings are joined ring to ring; an unnamed poet uses مسرودتان for two such coats.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r1.anchor: ويقال للدرع: مسرودة، لأنه توبع فيها الحلق بالحلق، قال الشاعر: وعليهما مسرودتان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r2.claim: The armor maker is called sarād or zarād, with s changing to z as in sirāṭ/zirāṭ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r2.anchor: ويقال لصانع ذلك: سراد وزراد، تبدل من السين الزاي كما قالوا: سراط وزراط.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r3.claim: The verb sard applies to reading the Qurʾān rapidly and to speech delivered in quick sequence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p516/r3.anchor: وسرد القرآن، إذا حدر فيه والكلام إذا تابعه مستعجلا فيه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r17.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada say the iron became soft like wax.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p524/r17.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: صار كالشمع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the iron became dough-like and David worked it without fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r1.anchor: الحسن: كالعجين، وكان يعمله من غير نار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r2.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r2.claim: Al-Suddi compares the softened iron to wet clay, dough, and wax, moldable without fire or hammer blows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r2.anchor: وقال السدي: كالطين المبلول والعجين والشمع، يصرفه كيف شاء من غير نار ولا ضرب مطرقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r3.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r3.claim: Al-Suddi compares the softened iron to wet clay, dough, and wax, moldable without fire or hammer blows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: كالطين المبلول والعجين والشمع، يصرفه كيف شاء من غير نار ولا ضرب مطرقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r4.claim: Another view says David was granted a power by which he could soften iron.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r4.anchor: وقيل: أعطي قوة يلين بها الحديد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r5.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r5.claim: Muqatil reports that David could complete armor in part of a day or night, worth a thousand dirhams; disguised, he asked an angel in human form about himself and heard that he relied on public funds instead of his own work.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: وكان يفرغ من الدرع في بعض يوم أو في بعض ليلة ثمنها ألف درهم، وكان داود يتنكر فيسأل الناس عن حاله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r6.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r6.claim: After the angel's criticism, David prayed for a craft; God taught him armor-making and softened iron, making him wealthy, and he spent a third of his wealth on Muslim public needs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r6.anchor: فدعا الله أن يعلمه صنعة ويسهلها عليه، فعلمه صنعة الدروع وألان له الحديد فأثرى، وكان ينفق ثلث المال في مصالح المسلمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r7.claim: An in an taʿmal is a masdariyya after a deleted preposition: God softened iron for making complete coats of mail.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r7.anchor: وأن في أن اعمل مصدرية، وهي على إسقاط حرف الجر، أي ألناه لعمل سابغات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r8.speaker: الحوفي وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r8.claim: Al-Hawfi and others allow an to be explanatory, but Abu Hayyan says that construction requires an antecedent with the sense of speech, absent here; positing an omitted command is unnecessary.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r8.anchor: وأجاز الحوفي وغيره أن تكون مفسرة، ولا يصح، لأن من شرطها أن يتقدمها معنى القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r9.claim: The reading ṣābighāt with ṣād instead of sīn is a dialect variant, previously noted in the phrase “He lavished His favors upon you.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r9.anchor: وقرىء: صابغات، بالصاد بدلا من السين، وتقدم أنها لغة في قوله: وأسبغ عليكم نعمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says to size each mail ring properly: too small weakens the armor, while too large leaves openings for an attack.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r10.anchor: قال ابن زيد: هو في قدر الحلقة، أي لا تعملها صغيرة فتضعف، فلا يقوى الدرع على الدفاع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas applies the instruction to rivets: neither make them thin enough to break nor thick enough to split; the final verb has fāʾ and qāf variants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو في المسمار، لا يرق فينكسر، ولا يغلظ فيفصم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r12.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r12.claim: Qatada says armor had previously been heavy plates, and David was the first to make linked mail.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p526/r12.anchor: وقال قتادة: إن الدروع كانت قبل صفائح كانت ثقالا، وهو أول من صنع الدرع حلقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528/r6.speaker: بعض الباطنية أو من يشبههم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528/r6.claim: The same interpreters reduce softening iron and flowing copper to ordinary extraction using fire and tools.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528/r6.anchor: وإلانة الحديد وإسالة القطر هو استخراج ذوبهما بالنار واستعمال الآلات منهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528#2/r5.claim: The successive commands to make armor, do righteous deeds, and work in gratitude teach that people must not become absorbed in worldly adornment but should act righteously.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p528#2/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الإنسان لا يستغرق في الدنيا ولا يلتفت إلى زخارفها، وأنه يجب أن يعمل صالحا

STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r10.claim: After its critique of disbelievers, the sūrah briefly recalls the accomplishments of David and Solomon.
STUDYQURAN:34:intro/r10.anchor: Brief allusions to the accomplishments of the prophets David (vv. 10–11) and Solomon (vv. 12–14)

SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r1.claim: The stronger analysis makes أن مصدرية after an omitted preposition ل, yielding لأن اعمل.
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r1.anchor: قوله: { أن اعمل }: فيها وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها مصدرية على حذف الحرف أي: لأن.

SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r2.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r2.claim: Al-Hawfi and others call أن explanatory, but that needs a preceding expression of speech, absent after ألنا; inventing وأمرناه is needless.
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r2.anchor: والثاني قاله الحوفي وغيره أنها مفسرة. ورد هذا: بأن شرطها تقدم ما هو بمعنى القول ولم يتقدم إلا " ألنا ".

SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r3.claim: A reading has صابغات to accommodate غين; its explanation was discussed at Luqman under وأسبغ.
SAMIN-DURR:34:11/r3.anchor: وقرئ " صابغات " لأجل الغين. وتقدم تقريره في لقمان عند " وأسبغ ".

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r3.claim: أن is explanatory: God softened the iron by telling David to make ample armor; it can also express purpose, “so that he make” armor.
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r3.anchor: في تأويل التفسير كأنه قيل: وألنا له الحديد أن أعمل

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r4.claim: أن can connect to an imperative in two senses: “he told him, rise,” or “he sent him so that he would rise.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r4.anchor: وتصل إن بلفظ الأمر، ومثل هذا من الكلام أرسل إليه

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r5.claim: سابغات means full, ample coats of mail; the adjective stands for the omitted noun, and describes armor covering its wearer with extra length.
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r5.anchor: دروع سابغات فذكر الصفة لأنها تدل على الموصوف

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r6.claim: In ordinary language, سرد is arranging things in sequence, one after another; the same root describes narrating speech in order.
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r6.anchor: السرد في اللغة تقدمة شيء إلى شيء تأتي به منسقا بعضه في إثر بعض

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r7.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r7.claim: Tafsīr explains السرد as fastening, covering, or making armor, and also as balancing rivet and hole sizes so the armor does not loosen, break, or snap.
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r7.anchor: وقيل في التفسير: السرد السمر والستر والخلق وقيل هو

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r8.claim: “Measure the chain” means make it moderate and proportionate to the need; the tafsīr account fits the language because fastening joins one end of a ring to the other.
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r8.anchor: قدر في ذلك أي اجعله على القصد وقدر الحاجة.

ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r9.speaker: سيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r9.claim: Sībawayh derives سرندي, “bold,” from سرد because a bold person presses forward.
ZAJJAJ:v4p243/r9.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن قول العرب: رجل سرندي مشتق من السرد،

ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n13/r1.claim: Sabigh means ample, abundant, or complete; plural sabighat functions as a noun for abundant, perfect deeds, supported by the related verb asbagha at 31:20.
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n13/r1.anchor: The adjective sabigh (fem. sabighan) signifies anything that is "ample", "abundant" and "complete"

ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n13/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n13/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n13/r2.claim: Sard denotes a consecutive continuation, with parts or stages following steadily, continuing, or repeating.
ASAD-NOTES:34:10#n13/r2.anchor: The noun sard, on the other hand, denotes something "carried on consecutively", or something the parts (or stages) whereof are "following one another steadily"

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r2.claim: Qatada explains the full-length garments as complete coats of armor.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ وألنا له الحديد ﴾ قال لينه الله له يعمله بغير نار وقوله ﴿ أن اعمل سابغات ﴾ يقول دروع سابغات

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the links in the armor are the nails used to join its rings.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ وقدر في السرد ﴾ قال السرد المسامير التي في حلق الدرع

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas instructs the maker not to use nails or rings that are too loose or too tight, but to proportion their size so the armor neither slips nor breaks.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p127#2/r4.anchor: ابن مجاهد عن أبيه عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ وقدر في السرد ﴾ قال لا تدق في المسامير وتوسع الحلقة فتسلس ولا تغلظ المسامير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r1.claim: He reads أن as a subjunctive verbal noun with an omitted preposition, preferably “for making complete coats of mail”; “He commanded him to make” is another estimate.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r1.anchor: مصدرية وهي على إسقاط حرف الجر

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r2.speaker: الحوفي وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r2.claim: They allow أن as an explanatory particle, although this requires a preceding sense of speech; some posit an omitted command, but deleting its explanatory verb is unattested.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r2.anchor: وأجاز الحوفي وغيره أن تكون مفسرة ولما كان شرط المفسرة أن يتقدمها معنى القول

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r3.claim: سابغات means coats of mail; it originally described completeness and fullness, then became a conventional name for mail.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r3.anchor: والسابغات الدروع وأصله صفة من السبوغ وهو التمام والكمال فغلب على الدروع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r4.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r4.claim: An anonymous poetic line uses سابغات for protective mail.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r4.anchor: لا سابغات ولا جأواء باسلة تقي المنون لدى إستيفاء آجال

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r5.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r5.claim: Another poem uses the plural سوابغ for white mail that arrows cannot pierce.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r5.anchor: عليها أسود ضاريات لبوسهم سوابغ بيض لا تخرقها النبل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r6.claim: No omitted noun such as “coats” is needed before سابغات; this does not refute the rule against deleting an adjective’s noun unless the adjective is distinctive.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r6.anchor: فلا حاجة إلى تقدير موصوف أي دروعا سابغات ولا يرد هذا نقصا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r7.speaker: قارئ
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r7.claim: A reading replaces sīn with ṣād in صابغات, assimilating the sound to the following ghayn.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r8.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r8.claim: Rāghib explains سرد as interlacing or stitching something rough and thick; the term is extended to the making of iron links.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r8.anchor: السرد نسج في الأصل كما قال الراغب خرز ما يخشن ويغلظ

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r9.speaker: الشماخ
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r9.claim: Al-Shammākh’s phrase سرد العنان uses سرد for successive stringing or interlacing, evidence for the root sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r9.anchor: قال الشماخ فظلت سراعا خيلنا في بيوتكم كما تابعت سرد العنان الخوارز

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r10.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r10.claim: Al-Baḥr glosses سرد as following one thing with another of its kind; a mail coat is linked because its rings follow one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r10.anchor: وفي البحر هو إتباع الشيء بالشيء من جنسه ويقال للدرع مسرودة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r11.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r11.claim: A poem describes two coats as مسرودتان, exemplifying mail formed by linked rings.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r11.anchor: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما داؤد أو صنع السوابغ تبع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in reports cited by al-Ṭabarī, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim, explains the command as making the rings proportionate.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r12.anchor: وإبن عباس فيما أخرجه عنه إبن جرير وإبن المنذر وإبن أبي حاتم من طرق بالحلق

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd says to avoid rings so small that the armor is weak and so large that gaps leave its wearer exposed.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r13.anchor: لا تعملها صغيرة فتضعف فلا يقوى الدرع على الدفاع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r14.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās, also attributed to Qatāda and Mujāhid, takes سرد as rivets: size them to fit the holes, neither too thin to hold nor too thick to tear the rings.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r14.anchor: وجاء في رواية أخرى عن إبن عباس تفسيرها بالمسامير وروى ذلك عن قتادة ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r15.claim: Al-Ālūsī questions the rivet explanation because softened iron could have its ring ends fused like wax or dough, making a stronger join without rivets; if the report is sound, David may have joined rings without fusing them.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r15.anchor: ويبعد هذا أن إلانة الحديد له عليه السلام بحيث كان كالشمع والعجين يغني عن التسمير

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r16.speaker: البقاعي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r16.claim: Al-Biqāʿī reports an unnamed observer’s claim that David’s armor had no rivets; al-Ālūsī dismisses it because the informant is unidentified.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r16.anchor: ما نقل عن البقاعي أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r17.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r17.claim: Another gloss limits armor-making to the amount needed for a livelihood, leaving the rest of David’s time for worship; it fits the following command.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r17.anchor: لا تصرف جميع أوقاتك فيه بل مقدار ما يحصل به القوت

ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r18.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r18.claim: A report from Qatāda says David was the first to make ringed mail; before him, armor was made of solid plates.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p114#3/r18.anchor: وحكى أنه عليه السلام أول من صنع الدرع حلقا وكانت قبل صفائح وروى ذلك عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r1.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r1.claim: Muqātil reports that, when David ruled Israel, an angel disguised as a man said he was virtuous except that he lived from the treasury; David prayed to learn a trade, was taught armor-making, prospered, and sold a coat for 1,000 dirhams.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r1.anchor: وعن مقاتل أنه عليه السلام حين ملك على بني إسرائيل يخرج متنكرا فيسأل الناس عن حاله

ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r2.speaker: ابن شوذب
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r2.claim: Ibn Shawdhab reports that David made one coat daily and sold it for 6,000 dirhams, keeping 2,000 for his household and spending 4,000 to feed Israelites fine white bread.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r2.anchor: عن إبن شوذب قال : كان داؤد عليه السلام يرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r3.claim: Another account says David sold each coat for 4,000 dirhams, supporting his family and giving alms to the poor.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r3.anchor: وقيل : كان يبيع الدرع بأربعة آلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r4.speaker: الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r4.claim: Al-Ṣādiq is cited in Majmaʿ al-Bayān as saying David made 360 coats and sold them for 360,000 dirhams, becoming independent of the public treasury.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r4.anchor: وفي مجمع البيان عن الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه عمل ثلثمائة وستين درعا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r5.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r5.claim: Al-Khafājī takes the address as David and his family, understood by implication from the mention of David.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r5.anchor: وهم وإن لم يجر لهم ذكر يفهمون على ما قال الخفاجي إلتزاما من ذكره

ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r6.claim: Another view makes David alone the addressee, with the plural form honoring him.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يكون خطابا له عليه السلام خاصة على سبيل التعظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r7.claim: Either way, the apparent command is to do righteous deeds generally; if addressed only to David, it is not merely a command to make flawless armor.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r7.anchor: وأياما كان فالظاهر أنه أمر بالعمل الصالح مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r8.claim: God’s seeing their deeds means He will recompense them, explaining the command or its binding force and motivating obedience through encouragement and warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p115/r8.anchor: فأجازيكم به وهو تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب الإمتثال به

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r1.claim: Sābighāt are complete, wide, long coats of mail that trail on the ground.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r1.anchor: دروعا كوامل واسعات طوالا تسحب في الأرض،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r2.claim: Sard is armor weaving; its maker is called a sarrād or zarrād.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r2.anchor: نسج الدروع، يقال لصانعه: السراد والزراد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r3.claim: Nails must fit the rings: too thin and they slip out, too thick and they break the rings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r3.anchor: يقول: قدر المسامير في حلق الدرع أي: لا تجعل المسامير دقاقا فتفلت ولا غلاظا فتكسر الحلق،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r4.claim: Sard can also mean the nail in a ring; a masrūda coat has nailed rings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r4.anchor: ويقال: "السرد" المسمار في الحلقة، يقال: درع مسرودة أي: مسمورة الحلق،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r5.claim: The command is to keep the armor work moderate and proportionate to need.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r6.claim: The plural command to do good is addressed to David and his family.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p388#2/r6.anchor: يريد: داود وآله، {إني بما تعملون بصير}

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r1.claim: God commanded David to make the coats; أن may be explanatory or infinitive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r1.anchor: أمرناه أن اعمل ف { أن } مفسرة أو مصدرية.

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r2.claim: They are broad coats of mail; a variant reads صابغات, and David was the first to make them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r2.anchor: دروعا واسعات، وقرىء «صابغات» وهو أول من اتخذها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r3.claim: David should regulate the weaving so the mail rings fit proportionately.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r3.anchor: وقدّر في نسجها بحيث يتناسب حلقها، أو قدّر مساميرها

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r4.claim: A view regulates rivets so they are neither thin and loose nor thick and splitting; Bayḍāwī rejects it because David’s mail was not riveted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r4.anchor: ورد بأن دروعه لم تكن مسمرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r5.claim: The plural command addresses David and his household.

BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r6.claim: God sees what they do and will reward them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:34:11-12/r6.anchor: إني بما تعملون بصير } فأجازيكم عليه.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r14.claim: The command to make armor explains the purpose of softening iron and indicates that David’s craft was devoted to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r14.anchor: ثم ذكر علة الإلانة بصيغة الأمر إشارة إلى أن عمله كان لله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r15.claim: Sābighāt are long, ample coats of armor.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r16.claim: Sard is the piercing and threading of leather; linking each armor ring to the next resembles stitching through holes with a continuous thread.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p157#2/r16.anchor: السرد الخزر في الأديم وإدخال الخيط في موضع الخرز

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r1.claim: David should make every ring equal and tight enough to stop arrows, secure against swords, and light enough for quick movement and fighting in hot or cold weather.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r1.anchor: أي النسج بأن يكون كل حلقة مساوية لأختها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r2.claim: Biqāʿī thinks the armor rings probably had no rivets: pliable iron made them unnecessary, and rivets would remove the benefit of softening; someone who saw the armor reportedly confirmed this.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنه لم يكن في حلقها مسامير لعدم الحاجة بإلانة الحديد إليها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines sard as measuring one thing to fit the next so that the parts follow in orderly succession, as in telling a story.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : السرد في اللغة : تقدير الشيء إلى الشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r4.claim: Biqāʿī compares David’s softened iron with the Prophet’s miraculous softening of the trench obstruction: one account says a single blow broke it, another says water made it loose sand.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r4.anchor: وهذا كما ألان الله تعالى للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الخندق تلك الكدية وفي رواية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r5.speaker: سلمان
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r5.claim: Salman reported that picks and axes failed against a rock at the trench; the Prophet broke it with three blows, each illuminating Medina, and announced the future conquests of Ṣanʿāʾ, al-Ḥīra, and Syria.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r5.anchor: تلك الصخرة التي أخبره سلمان رضي الله عنها أنها كسرت فؤوسهم ومعاولهم وعجزوا عنها فضربها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث ضربات

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن جحش
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r6.claim: Biqāʿī cites a report, noted by al-Kilāʿī from al-Zubayr b. Abī Bakr and al-Bayhaqī, that the Prophet turned ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaḥsh’s broken Uhud sword into a palm rib sword called al-ʿAwn, later sold for 200 dinars.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r6.anchor: سيف عبد الله بن جحش رضي الله عنه انقطع يوم أحد , فأعطاه رسول الله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r7.speaker: عكاشة بن محصن
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r7.claim: At Badr, the Prophet gave ʿUkāsha b. Miḥṣan a piece of wood when his sword broke; it became a long, strong, bright sword, which he carried in later campaigns until his death in the Ridda.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r7.anchor: وقاتل عكاشة بن محصن يوم بدر فانقطع سيفه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r8.speaker: الواقدي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r8.claim: Al-Wāqidī reports that when Salama b. Aslam b. al-Ḥuraysh’s sword broke at Badr, the Prophet gave him a date-palm twig that became a fine sword, kept until Salama died at the Battle of the Bridge.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r8.anchor: وعن الواقدي أنه انكسر سيف سلمة بن أسلم بن الحريش يوم بدر فأعطاه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r9.speaker: معوذ بن عفراء
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r9.claim: Biqāʿī cites al-Bayhaqī and others on the Prophet restoring Muʿawwidh b. ʿAfrāʾ’s severed hand after Abū Jahl cut it at Badr; it healed as before.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r9.anchor: وإلحامه للحديد ليس بأعجب من إلحام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليد معوذ بن عفراء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r10.claim: The plural command turns from favors particular to David to a command that includes him and everyone who obeys him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r10.anchor: عطف عليها ما جمع فيه الضمير لأنه يعم غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r11.claim: David and his followers should do right by means of the knowledge and divinely granted success to obey that God has given them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r11.anchor: أي بما تفضلنا به عليكم من العلم والتوفيق للطاعة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r12.claim: God sees and knows every deed, inward and outward; this assurance encourages obedience and warns against neglect.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r12.anchor: أي مبصر وعالم بكل ظاهر له وباطن

BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r13.claim: The emphatic warning answers denials of resurrection, which imply denial of other divine attributes; the negligent act as though they deny that God observes them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p158/r13.anchor: إشارة إلى أن إنكارهم للقدرة على البعث إنكار لغيرها من الصفات

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r4.claim: Qatada says David shaped softened iron by hand like clay into linked armor without fire or hammering; he was the first to make such armor, whereas earlier people used iron plates for protection.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وألنا له الحديد} قال: لين الله له الحديد فكان يسرده حلقا بيده يعمل به كما يعمل بالطين من غير أن يدخله النار ولا يضربه بمطرقة

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r5.claim: Hasan says the iron became dough-like in David’s hand so he could make armor from it.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r5.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {وألنا له الحديد} فيصير في يده مثل العجين فيصنع منه الدروع

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ‘the linked work’ as the iron rings of the armor.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r6.anchor: من طرق عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وقدر في السرد} قال: حلق الحديد

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r7.claim: Qatada explains the term as the rivets that join the rings.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {وقدر في السرد} قال: السرد المسامير التي في الحلق

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas instructs making the rivets and rings proportionate: neither thin, loose rivets and wide links nor thick rivets and narrow links that break.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وقدر في السرد} قال: لا تدق المسامير وتوسع الحلق فتسلسل ولا تغلظ المسامير

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r9.claim: Mujahid says to measure rivets and rings carefully so the rivets neither slide through nor leave the links liable to break.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {وقدر في السرد} قال: قدر المسامير والحلق لا تدق المسمار فيسلسل ولا تحلها

DURR-FULL:v6p675/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r10.speaker: ابن شوذب
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r10.claim: Ibn Shudhdb says David made one coat of armor each day and sold it for six thousand dirhams: two thousand for his household and four thousand to feed the Israelites sifted bread.
DURR-FULL:v6p675/r10.anchor: عن ابن شوذب رضي الله عنه قال: كان داود عليه السلام يرفع في كل يوم درعا فيبيعها بستة آلاف درهم ألفين له ولأهله وأربعة آلاف يطعم بها بني إسرائيل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the links in the mail as iron rings.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : وقدر في السرد قال : حلق الحديد

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r5.claim: Qatada explains the links in the mail as the nails in its rings.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3162/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : وقدر في السرد قال : السرد : المسامير التي في الحلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r10.claim: An is explanatory: making iron pliable implied that God inspired David to use it by making full coats of mail.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p155/r10.anchor: و { أن } تفسيرية لما في { ألنا له } من معنى : أشعرناه بتسخير الحديد ليقدم على صنعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r2.claim: Sābighāt is an adjective whose omitted noun, coats of mail, is obvious because armor is conventionally described as full or ample.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r2.anchor: وسابغات } صفة لموصوف محذوف لظهوره من المقام إذ شاع وصف الدروع بالسابغات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r3.claim: Qaddir means to set something to a particular measure or proportion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r3.anchor: ومعنى { قدر } اجعله على تقدير ، والتقدير : جعل الشيء على مقدار مخصوص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r4.claim: Sard is making mail armor by linking its rings and rivets, the metal equivalent of sewing cloth; armor is called both masrūd and sābigh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r4.anchor: و { السرد } صنع درع الحديد ، أي تركيب حلقها ومساميرها التي تشد شقق الدرع بعضها ببعض فهي للحديد كالخياطة للثوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r5.speaker: أبو ذؤيب الهذلي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r5.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb’s line uses masrūdatān for two coats of mail, illustrating the armor sense of sard.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r5.anchor: قال أبو ذؤيب الهذلي : وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما داود أو صنع السوابغ تبع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r6.speaker: المعري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r6.claim: Al-Maʿarrī’s description of David as maker of full armor is another poetic witness to the armor usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r6.anchor: وقال المعري يصف درعا : وداود قين السابغات أذالها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r7.claim: The maker of armor is called sarrād or zarrād, with either sīn or zāy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r7.anchor: ويقال لناسج الدروع : سراد وزراد بالسين والزاي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r8.claim: After granting David what others find difficult, God commands righteous work as gratitude, since thanks are shown by acts pleasing to the benefactor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r8.anchor: فلما سخر الله له ما استصعب على غيره أتبعه بأمره بالشكر بأن يعمل صالحا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r9.claim: The plural command may address David and his family, as in Ṭā Hā 20:132, or address David alone honorifically.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p156/r9.anchor: وضمير { اعملوا } لداود وآله كقوله تعالى : { وأمر أهلك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها } ( طه : 132 ) أو له وحده على وجه التعظيم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p157/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p157/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p157/r1.claim: Inna here functions like a causal fa, as in Bashshār’s line ‘Indeed, success lies in rising early’; Ibn ʿĀshūr says he explained this elsewhere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p157/r1.anchor: موقع ( إن ) فيه موقع فاء التسبب كقول بشار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p157/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p157/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p157/r2.claim: Baṣīr means fully informed and knowing; here it alludes to recompense for righteous work.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v22p157/r2.anchor: والبصير : المطلع العليم ، وهو هنا كناية عن الجزاء عن العمل الصالح

BURSEVI:v7p209/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r4.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines sabagha as extending down to the ground; a complete, long coat of mail is sābighah, and the root is also used of an ample ablution or blessing.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r4.anchor: سبغ الشيء سبوغا طال إلى الأرض والنعمة انسبغت ودرع سابغة تامة طويلة

BURSEVI:v7p209/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r5.claim: David was the first to make coats of mail; armor had previously consisted of beaten flat iron plates.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r5.anchor: وهو عليه السلام أول من اتخذها وكانت قبل ذلك صفائح حديد مضروبة

BURSEVI:v7p209/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r7.claim: The account says David made one coat of mail daily, sold it for four or six thousand dirhams, kept two thousand for his family, and gave the rest to Israel’s poor.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r7.anchor: فكان يعمل كل يوم درعا ويبيعها بأربعة آلاف درهم أو بستة آلاف ينفق عليه وعلى عياله ألفين ويتصدق بالباقي

BURSEVI:v7p209/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r8.claim: A hadith says David ate only from the earnings of his own hand.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r8.anchor: كان داود لا يأكل إلا من كسب يده

BURSEVI:v7p209/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r9.claim: The verse shows that people of distinction should learn crafts: working with one’s hands does not lower rank but adds merit through humility and independence.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r9.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على تعلم أهل الفضل الصنائع فإن العمل بها لا ينقص بمرتبتهم بل ذلك زيادة في فضلهم

BURSEVI:v7p209/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209/r10.claim: A hadith says the best food a person eats is what comes from the work of their own hand; Saʿdī’s verse similarly praises craft and dignity over reliance on wealth.
BURSEVI:v7p209/r10.anchor: إن خير ما أكل المرء من عمل يده

BURSEVI:v7p209/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209/r11.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
BURSEVI:v7p209/r11.claim: Saʿdī’s Persian poem says to teach a craft and preserve dignity: a purse of silver and gold empties, but a craft keeps earning.

BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r1.claim: Al-Mufradāt says sard first meant stitching rough, thick material such as leather, then came to mean linking iron and weaving coats of mail. A maker was called sarād or zarād, and linked speech is also called sard.
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r1.anchor: والسرد في الأصل خرز ما يخشن ويغلظ كخرز الجلد

BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r2.claim: Sard also means joining speech continuously, but such speech is acceptable only when it does not impair understanding.
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r2.anchor: وسرد كلامه وصل بعضه ببعض وأتى به متتابعا وهو إنما يكون مقبولا إذا لم يخل بالفهم

BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r3.claim: David should weave the armor economically, keeping its rings proportionate; he should not spend all his time on the craft, only enough to provide strength, and devote the rest to worship.
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r3.anchor: اقتصد في نسجها بحيث تناسب حلقها

BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r5.claim: The command to measure the linking signifies speaking wisdom in a measure suited to people’s understanding.
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r5.anchor: الحديث بأن تتكلم بالحكمة على قدر عقول الناس

BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r6.claim: A Persian couplet warns against offering fine points of wisdom to those unable to understand, like scattering jewels before a donkey.
BURSEVI:v7p209#2/r6.anchor: نكته كفتن يش كفهمان زحكمت بيكمان جوهرى ند ازجواهر ريختن يش خرست

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r1.claim: The plural command addresses David and his household because the obligation applies generally.

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r2.claim: Righteous work is sincere work, free from ulterior motives.

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r3.claim: God sees what they do and will not let any worker’s deed go unrewarded; this explains the command or why it must be obeyed.
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r3.anchor: لا أضيع عمل عامل منكم فأجازيكم عليه وهو تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب الامتثال به

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r4.claim: The Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya interprets the command as referring to every outward and inward faculty, each of which should perform the act of servitude suited to it and for which it was created.
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r4.anchor: إلى جميع أعضائه الظاهرة والباطنة أن تعمل في العبودية كل واحدة منها

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r5.claim: Al-Baṣīr perceives every existent through sight; one who knows this name monitors every movement and stillness, avoiding what God forbids and not neglecting what He commands.
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r5.anchor: والبصير هو المدرك لكل موجود برؤيته ومن عرف أنه البصير راقبه في الحركات والسكنات حتى لا يراه حيث نهاه

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r6.claim: The author says this divine name’s special effect is success: reciting it one hundred times before Friday prayer opens inward sight and guides speech and action, though people remain fallible.
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r6.anchor: وخاصية هذا الاسم وجود التوفيق فمن قرأه قبل صلاة الجمعة مائة مرة فتح الله بصيرته ووفقه لصالح القول والعمل

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r7.claim: A saying reports that David once prayed for wrongdoers not to be forgiven, from religious zeal; after his own lapse, he prayed for sinners to be forgiven.

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r8.claim: A story says that after David’s repentance, people, jinn, and birds gathered; when birds heard his voice but sensed his changed state, they flew away. God explained this estrangement as the effect of his lapse, unlike the intimacy of obedience.

BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r9.claim: A Persian couplet urges people to move only by God’s command and keep watch over obedience, since a step against His command brings a sharp reckoning.
BURSEVI:v7p209#3/r9.anchor: قدم نتوان نهاد آنجاكه خواهى بفرمان رو بفرمان كن نكاهى كه هر كاو نه بامر حق قدم زد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r14.claim: An is explained either as a particle introducing the command without syntactic position, or as accusative after an omitted preposition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r14.anchor: أن مفسرة لا موضع لها من الإعراب، وقيل هي في موضع نصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r15.claim: Sābighāt are full-covering coats of mail with extra coverage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r15.anchor: الدروع الكاسيات ذوات الفضول، قال قتادة داود عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r16.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r16.claim: Qatāda says David was the first to make chainmail.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r16.anchor: قال قتادة داود عليه السلام أول من صنعها، ودرع الحديد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r17.claim: Dirʿ (“armor”) is grammatically feminine for iron armor but masculine for a woman’s armor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r17.anchor: الحديد مؤنث ودرع المرأة مذكر، وقوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r18.claim: Sard is joining one item to another of the same kind, as in chain-links, recounting speech, or joining chainmail rings; the Shammākh line “as you followed the reins” witnesses the term.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r18.anchor: قال الشماخ: «كما تابعت سرد العنان الخوارز»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r19.claim: Mail is called masrūda because its rings are linked successively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p407/r19.anchor: وقيل للدرع مسرودة لأنها توبعت فيها الحلق بالحلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r1.claim: The cited line says the two coats of mail were joined; its wording illustrates the chainmail term.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r1.anchor: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما ... دواد أو صنع السوابغ تبع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r2.claim: Duraid’s Persian term for chainmail is al-masrad.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says to size each ring: too small weakens the armor, while too large leaves gaps through which its wearer can be struck.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r3.anchor: فقال ابن زيد: التقدير الذي أمر به هو في قدر الحلقة أي لا تعملها صغيرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the calibration to concern the nail joining the rings; the nail should neither slip through nor be so thick that it breaks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس التقدير الذي أمر به هو المسمار يريد ثقبه حين يشد نتيرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r5.claim: Qatāda says earlier armor consisted of heavy plates, so David was told to balance lightness with protection rather than maximize either alone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r5.anchor: وروى قتادة أن الدروع كانت قبله صفائح فكانت ثقالا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r6.claim: The command to act righteously also addresses David’s family, though they are not named, because context implies them; God sees good and evil and rewards accordingly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p408/r6.anchor: لما كان الأمر لداود وآله حكى وإن كانوا لم يجر لهم ذكر لدلالة المعنى عليهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads an iʿmal as an understood “We said to him: work,” or as expressing purpose, “so that he might work.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج معناه وقلنا له اعمل ويكون في معنى لأن يعمل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r2.claim: Sābighāt means complete suits of mail; the adjective stands for the armor it describes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r2.anchor: سابغات أي دروعا سابغات فذكر الصفة لانها تدل على الموصوف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r3.claim: Exegetes say David shaped iron like dough, made armor in part of a day, sold it for a great price, and used the proceeds to live and give charity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r3.anchor: كان يأخذ الحديد بيده فيصير كأنه عجين يعمل به ما يشاء فيعمل الدرع في بعض يوم فيبيعه بمال كثير فيأكل ويتصدق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r4.claim: The armor covered its wearer completely, with excess length dragging on the ground.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r4.anchor: والسابغات الدروع الكوامل التي تغطي لابسها حتى تفضل عنه فيجرها على الأرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r5.claim: The command is to make the mail links to a suitable measure.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba says sard is weaving; a mail maker is called sarrād or zarrād, with sibilants exchanging as in sirāṭ/ẕirāṭ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة السرد النسج ومنه يقال لصانع الدروع سراد وزراد تبدل من السين الزاي كما يقال سراط وزراط

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines sard as putting one thing after another in a connected sequence; the same root describes narrating speech continuously.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج السرد في اللغة تقدمة الشئ إلى الشئ تأني به متسقا بعضه في إثر بعض متتابعا ومنه قولهم سرد فلان الحديث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid says to size the nail in each link: too small makes it loose, while too large splits the ring.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r8.anchor: أحدهما عدل المسمار في الحلقة ولا تصغره فيقلق ولا تعظمه فتنفصم الحلقة قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r9.claim: Qatāda says not to make the links too wide, lest they fail to protect the wearer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p436#2/r9.anchor: والثاني لا تجعل حلقه واسعة فلا تقي صاحبها قاله قتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r3.claim: Qatada says David was the first human to make armor; before him, armor consisted of sheets or plates.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: وهو أول من عملها من الخلق، وإنما كانت قبل ذلك صفائح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r4.speaker: ابن شوذب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r4.claim: Ibn Shadhub reports that David sold one armor each day for six thousand dirhams, allocating two thousand to his family and four thousand to feed the Israelites.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r4.anchor: ابن شوذب قال: كان داود، عليه السلام، يرفع في كل يوم درعا فيبيعها بستة آلاف درهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r5.claim: The instruction to measure the links is God's guidance to David in the craft of making armor.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r5.anchor: هذا إرشاد من الله لنبيه داود، عليه السلام، في تعليمه صنعة الدروع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد، والحكم بن عتيبة، وقتادة وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r6.claim: Mujahid, al-Hakam ibn Utayba, Qatada, and others say to make each nail proportionate: too thin and it shakes, too thick and it splits the ring.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد في قوله: {وقدر في السرد} : لا تدق المسمار فيقلق في الحلقة، ولا تغلظه فيفصمها، واجعله بقدر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas defines al-sard as iron rings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: السرد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r8.claim: Some say a mail coat described as masrūda has its rings nailed together, citing an anonymous poet's line about two such coats made by David or Tubbʿ.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: يقال: درع مسرودة: إذا كانت مسمورة الحلق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r9.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r9.claim: Ibn Asakir transmits a report from Wahb through Isḥaq ibn Bishr, whom Ibn Kathir says has been criticized: David disguised himself to ask people about his rule, and an angel said he relied on public funds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r9.anchor: من طريق إسحاق بن بشر -وفيه كلام-عن أبي إلياس، عن وهب بن منبه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r10.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r10.claim: In Wahb's report, David prayed for a livelihood from his own hand, received softened iron and armor-making knowledge, then divided sales among charity, family needs, and later charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p497#2/r10.anchor: فعند ذلك نصب داود، عليه السلام، إلى ربه في الدعاء أن يعلمه عملا بيده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p498/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p498/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p498/r1.claim: David and his people are told to do righteous deeds in response to the blessings God gave them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p498/r1.anchor: أي: في الذي أعطاكم الله من النعم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p498/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p498/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p498/r2.claim: God watches them and sees all their deeds and words; nothing is hidden from Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p498/r2.anchor: أي: مراقب لكم، بصير بأعمالكم وأقوالكم، لا يخفى علي من ذلك شيء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r12.claim: A reading has ṣābighāt, an accusative plural form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r12.anchor: وقرىء : ( صابغات ) وهي الدروع الواسعة الضافية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r13.claim: The sābighāt are broad coats of mail; David first made them, whereas armor had been plates.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r13.anchor: وهي الدروع الواسعة الضافية ، وهو أول من اتخذها وكانت قبل صفائح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r14.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r14.claim: It is said David sold armor for four thousand, supporting his household while giving alms to the poor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r14.anchor: وقيل : كان يبيع الدرع بأربعة آلاف فينفق منها على نفسه وعياله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r15.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r15.claim: A story says David went incognito to ask about himself; an angel praised him except for family support from the treasury, so he asked God for a livelihood and was taught armor-making.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r15.anchor: وقيل : كان يخرج حين ملك بني إسرائيل متنكرا ، فيسأل الناس عن نفسه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r16.claim: Set armor nails to a proper size: thin ones loosen the links, thick ones split them; sard is the weaving of armor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r16.anchor: لا تجعل المسامير دقاقا فتقلق ، ولا غلاظا فتفصم الحلق . والسرد : نسج الدروع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p580#3/r17.claim: The plural command to do good is addressed to David and his household.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p435#2/r13.claim: Sābighāt means complete coats of armor, from the verb meaning to complete or make abundant; a poetic line describes complete armor and a piercing spear.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r1.claim: Mujahid says to balance nails and rings so armor does not slip or break.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r1.anchor: قاله مجاهد . الثاني : لا تجعل حلقه واسعة فلا تقي صاحبها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r2.claim: Qatada says not to make the rings too wide, so they protect the wearer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r2.anchor: لا تجعل حلقه واسعة فلا تقي صاحبها , قال قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r3.claim: Qatada says David first made chain mail; before him armor was made from plates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r3.anchor: قال قتادة : وكان داود أول من عملها , وكان قبل ذلك صفائح

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-sard means holes in mail rings; Labid's verse speaks of David's interwoven armor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r4.anchor: أنه النقب الذي في حلق الدرع , قاله ابن عباس , قال لبيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r5.claim: Qatada says al-sard means nails in armor rings, derived from stringing speech consecutively.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r5.anchor: أنه المسامير التي في حلق الدرع , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r6.claim: The Prophet described the sacred months as three consecutive and one separate, illustrating sard as succession.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r6.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : في الأشهر الحرم ثلاثة سرد وواحد فرد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r7.speaker: الهذلي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r7.claim: A Hudhali poem calls two coats of mail مسرودتان, evidence for sard's armor sense.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r8.speaker: ضمرة بن شوذب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r8.claim: Damra ibn Shawdhab says David sold one coat daily for 6,000 dirhams: 2,000 for family and 4,000 for Israelites' hawari bread.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r8.anchor: وحكى ضمرة بن شوذب أن داود عليه السلام كان يرفع كل يوم درعا فيبيعها بستة آلآف درهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r9.speaker: يحيى بن سلام والفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r9.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam and al-Farra say Luqman watched David make his first armor, wondered what it was, and waited to ask.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r9.anchor: وحكى يحيى بن سلام والفراء أن لقمان حضر داود عند أول درع عملها فجعل يتفكر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r10.speaker: لقمان
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r10.claim: When David wore it, Luqman called it excellent war protection and said silence is wisdom practiced by few.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r10.anchor: وقال : نعمت جنة الحرب هذه , فقال لقمان : الصمت حكمة وقليل فاعله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies righteous work as tasbih, praise, the declaration of God's oneness, and takbir.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r11.anchor: هو قول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r12.claim: Another explanation is to perform all acts of obedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r13.claim: God knows whatever people do, good or evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p436/r13.anchor: أي يعلم ما تعملون من خير أو شر

MUJAHID:v2p523#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p523#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p523#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says to proportion the rivets and rings: rivets must not be so fine that the links slip or so coarse that they split.
MUJAHID:v2p523#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وقدر في السرد ﴾ يقول قدر المسمار ( 1 ) والحلق لا تدق المسامير فتسلسل

MUQATIL:34:10-12/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r4.claim: Sabighat are long coats of mail. Earlier armor was hammered iron plates; David fastened mail with nails without hammering it with iron or heating it.
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r4.anchor: وكانت الدروع قبل داود إنما هي صفائح الحديد مضروبة

MUQATIL:34:10-12/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r5.claim: Size the nails to the mail: oversized nails break, while overly fine weaving lets them slip loose.
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r5.anchor: قدر المسامير في الخلق ولا تعظم المسامير فتنقصم

MUQATIL:34:10-12/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r6.claim: God’s instruction to David’s household to do good means that they should say, “Praise be to God.”
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r6.anchor: لآل داود: { واعملوا صالحا } يعني قولوا الحمد لله

MUQATIL:34:10-12/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:34:10-12/r7.claim: God sees what David’s household does.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r1.claim: An means that is: God commanded David to make armor.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r1.anchor: أن بمعنى أى أمرناه ان اعمل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r2.claim: Sabighat are full, spacious coats of mail, from a word for full extension.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r2.anchor: دروعا واسعة تامة من السبوغ وهو

NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r3.claim: David first made armor; he sold each coat for four thousand, supporting his family and giving to the poor.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r3.anchor: وهو أول من اتخذها وكان يبيع الدرع بأربعة آلاف فينفق منها على نفسه وعياله ويتصدق على الفقراء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r4.claim: An alternate story says an angel in human form criticized David for feeding his family from the public treasury; David prayed for self-sufficiency and God taught armor making.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r4.anchor: وقيل كان يخرج متنكرا فيسال الناس عن نفسه ويقول لهم ماتقولون فى داود فيثنون عليه فقيض الله له ملكا فى سورة آدمى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r5.claim: Adjust the weave: nails should not be so thin they loosen or so thick they split the rings; sard is armor weaving.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r5.anchor: لا نجعل المسامير دقاقا فنغلق ولا غلاظا فتفصم الحلق والسردنسج الدروع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r6.claim: The plural command addresses David and his family; they should act sincerely for acceptance, for God sees and recompenses their deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p322/r6.anchor: الضمير لداود وأهله ﴿ صالحا ﴾ خالصا يصلح للقبول

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r1.claim: Sābighāt are complete, full, spacious coats of armor; the root describes something covering the body and extending beyond it.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r1.anchor: أي دروعا سابغات، أي كوامل تامات واسعات

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r2.claim: Qatada says earlier armor was heavy plates, so David was told to balance lightness with protection.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: كانت الدروع قبله صفائح فكانت ثقالا

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the measure concerns ring size: rings must not be so small that the armor is weak or so large that they harm the wearer.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: التقدير الذي مر به هو في قدر الحلقة

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the measure concerns rivets: a thin one loosens the links and a thick one splits them; the text reports alternate verbs.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: التقدير الذي أمر به هو في المسمار

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r5.claim: Sard is the weaving of armor rings; its maker is called sarād or zarād, with sīn and zāy alternating as in sirāṭ and zirāṭ.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r5.anchor: السرد نسج حلق الدروع، ومنه قيل لصانع حلق الدروع: السراد والزراد، تبدل من السين الزاي

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r6.claim: Sard also means sewing: sarada yasrudu means to sew, and a misrad is an awl; sarād can mean the thong used for sewing.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r6.anchor: والسرد: الخرز، يقال: سرد يسرد إذا خرز. والمسرد: الإشفى، ويقال سراد

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r7.speaker: الشماخ
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r7.claim: Al-Shammakh's line uses sard for consecutive stitching of reins, illustrating the sewing sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r7.anchor: قال الشماخ: فظلت تباعا خيلنا في بيوتكم

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r8.claim: Sard also describes speech or fasting done consecutively in an unbroken sequence.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r8.anchor: ويقال: قد سرد الحديث والصوم فالسرد فيهما أن يجيء بهما

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r9.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r9.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet did not speak in a rapid unbroken sequence; he spoke distinctly enough to be counted.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r9.anchor: وفي حديث عائشة: لم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يسرد الحديث

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r10.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r10.claim: Sibawayh says sarandā means a bold person because he presses forward; the image derives from armor rings joined in order.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r10.anchor: قال سيبويه: ومنه رجل سرندى أي جريء، قال: لأنه يمضي قدما

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r11.speaker: لبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r11.claim: Labid's line describes iron made with doubled rings, exemplifying mail construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r11.anchor: قال لبيد: صنع الحديد مضاعفا أسراده

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r12.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r12.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb describes two garments of mail made by David or a Tubbaʿ, using masrūdatān for linked armor.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11/r12.anchor: وقال أبو ذؤيب: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما داود

QURTUBI-FULL:34:11#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11#2/r1.claim: The command means to perform righteous deeds and is addressed to David and his household, as in the command to the House of David to work in gratitude.
QURTUBI-FULL:34:11#2/r1.anchor: أي عملا صالحا. وهذا خطاب لداود وأهله

QASHANI:34:10-11/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:34:10-11/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:34:10-11/r5.claim: The ample coats of mail symbolize forms of scrupulous piety, a protective garment against the soul's hostile impulses and Satan's arrows.
QASHANI:34:10-11/r5.anchor: من هيئات الورع والتقوى فإن الورع الحصين في الحقيقة هو لباس الورع الحافظ من صوارم دواعي أعادي النفوس

QASHANI:34:10-11/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:34:10-11/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:34:10-11/r6.claim: Proportioning the links signifies practical wisdom and skilled rational and religious craft that encourages purifying deeds and forms that prevent the soul's promptings from taking effect.
QASHANI:34:10-11/r6.anchor: بالحكمة العملية والصنعة المتقنة العقلية والشرعية في ترغيب الأعمال المزكية

QASHANI:34:10-11/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:34:10-11/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:34:10-11/r7.claim: The command addresses those working for God, gathering from the lower realm toward the upper; righteous work raises them toward the divine presence and prepares them to receive holy lights. David is the spirit with its faculties and bodily members.
QASHANI:34:10-11/r7.anchor: أيها العاملون لله بالجمعية في الجهة السفلية إلى الجهة العلوية عملا صالحا يصعدكم في الترقي إلى الحضرة الإلهية

TAB-FULL:v19p222/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r4.claim: Sābighāt are complete, ample coats of mail; the instruction to David was to make full armor.
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r4.anchor: وعهدنا إليه أن اعمل سابغات، وهي التوام الكوامل من الدروع

TAB-FULL:v19p222/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r5.claim: Qatāda says sābighāt are coats of mail, which David was the first to make; before him people used plates.
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {أن اعمل سابغات} [سبأ: 11] ": دروع، وكان أول من صنعها داود، إنما كان قبل ذلك صفائح

TAB-FULL:v19p222/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses sābighāt as iron armor.
TAB-FULL:v19p222/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {أن اعمل سابغات} [سبأ: 11] قال: " السابغات: دروع الحديد

TAB-FULL:v19p223/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r1.claim: Qatada explains sard as the nails joining armor rings and describes making armor without fire or striking it with iron.
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {وقدر في السرد} [سبأ: 11] قال: " كان يجعلها بغير نار، ولا يقرعها بحديد، ثم يسردها والسرد: المسامير التي في الحلق

TAB-FULL:v19p223/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says sard means the ring itself and cites a poem about widening and perfecting rings.
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله : {وقدر في السرد} [سبأ: 11] قال: " السرد: حلقة؛ أي قدر تلك الحلق " قال: وقال الشاعر:

TAB-FULL:v19p223/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains sard as perforating armor and closing its gaps.
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وقدر في السرد} [سبأ: 11] " يعني بالسرد: ثقب الدروع فيسد قتيرها

TAB-FULL:v19p223/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r4.claim: Some Arabic scholars say ringed armor is called masruda and cite a poem about two coats of armor as evidence.
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r4.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب: يقال درع مسرودة: إذا كانت مسمورة الحلق؛ واستشهد لقيله ذلك بقول الشاعر

TAB-FULL:v19p223/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r5.claim: Qatada reports that armor had been plates before David was commanded to make it from linked rings.
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {وقدر في السرد} [سبأ: 11] قال: «كانت صفائح، فأمر أن يسردها حلقا»

TAB-FULL:v19p223/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r6.claim: Nails and rings must be sized properly: thick nails split rings, while small thin nails slip through.
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r6.anchor: وعنى بقوله {وقدر في السرد} [سبأ: 11] وقدر المسامير في حلق الدروع حتى يكون بمقدار لا تغلظ المسمار

TAB-FULL:v19p223/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r7.claim: Mujahid says to size nails and rings so nails neither slip through nor split the rings.
TAB-FULL:v19p223/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وقدر في السرد} [سبأ: 11] قال: «قدر المسامير والحلق، لا تدق المسامير فتسلس، ولا تجلها»

TAB-FULL:v19p226/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p226/r1.speaker: الحكم
TAB-FULL:v19p226/r1.claim: Al-Hakam says not to make a nail thick enough to split the ring or hammer it so thin that it splits.
TAB-FULL:v19p226/r1.anchor: عن الحكم، في قوله: {وقدر في السرد} [سبأ: 11] قال: «لا تغلظ المسمار فيفصم الحلقة، ولا تدقه فيفلق»

TABATABAI:34:10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10/r1.claim: The passage recalls God's favors to David and Solomon and commands righteous work in gratitude: David received mountains, birds, and pliable iron; Solomon received the wind and obedient jinn.
TABATABAI:34:10/r1.anchor: إذ آتاهما الله من فضله إذ أنعم على داود بتسخير الجبال والطير معه

TABATABAI:34:10-12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r2.claim: Sābighāt are ample coats of mail; sard is their linked-ring weaving, and qaddir means to keep its rings proportionate.
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r2.anchor: السابغات جمع سابغة وهي الدرع الواسعة

TABATABAI:34:10-12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r3.claim: The command to make ample, proportioned mail explains how God made iron pliable for David.

TABATABAI:34:10-12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r4.claim: In the context of describing a favor, the command to David and his people to act righteously means to thank God through good works.
TABATABAI:34:10-12/r4.anchor: وهي لوقوعها في سياق بيان إيتاء الفضل وعد النعم تفيد معنى الأمر بالشكر

TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r2.claim: Sābigh means ample or complete clothing; sard of iron means ordering its links, from the sense of following one part of speech after another.
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r2.anchor: والسابغ التام من اللباس وسرد الحديد نظمه

TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r3.claim: An unattributed poem describes a sound, tightly woven coat of mail; Abū Dhuʾayb describes two coats of mail made by David or by armor makers.
TABRISI:34:10-14#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو ذؤيب: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما داود

TABRISI:34:11-14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-14/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-14/r2.claim: An is explanatory, equivalent to “that is”; the implied wording is “We said: make complete coats of mail,” or it may mean “in order to make.” This an can precede a command.
TABRISI:34:11-14/r2.anchor: أن ها هنا في تأويل التفسير والقول وهي تدعي المفسرة بمعنى أي

TABRISI:34:11-14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-14/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-14/r3.claim: The object of “measure” is omitted and understood as the rings and nails of the mail.
TABRISI:34:11-14/r3.anchor: وقدر مفعوله محذوف أي قدر الحلق والمسامير

TABRISI:34:11-14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-14/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-14/r6.claim: Shukran can be a cognate accusative, understood as “give thanks, thanking”; alternatively it is purpose, with “obedience” understood as the object of “do.”
TABRISI:34:11-14/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مفعول اعملوا على تقدير اشكروا شكرا كما تقول أحمد الله

TABRISI:34:11-12/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-12/r4.claim: God told David to make complete coats of mail from iron; He softened it and taught him the craft because David wanted to live by his own work.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r4.anchor: أي قلنا له اعمل من الحديد دروعا تامات وإنما ألان الله تعالى الحديد لداود لأنه أحب أن يأكل من كسب يده

TABRISI:34:11-12/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-12/r5.claim: David was the first to make armor; he sold it, fed his family, and gave charity from the proceeds.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r5.anchor: وعلمه صنعة الدرع وكان أول من اتخذها وكان يبيعها ويأكل من ثمنها

TABRISI:34:11-12/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r6.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:34:11-12/r6.claim: Al-Sadiq reports that God praised David but reproached him for eating from the public treasury; David wept forty mornings, then made 360 coats, selling them for 360,000 dirhams and becoming self-sufficient.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r6.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع قال: إن الله أوحى إلى داود ع نعم العبد أنت إلا أنك تأكل

TABRISI:34:11-12/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-12/r7.claim: Sabighat means complete, full-coverage coats of mail.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r7.anchor: أي قلنا له اعمل من الحديد دروعا تامات

TABRISI:34:11-12/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-12/r8.claim: Sard is the interweaving of armor; its maker is called a sarrad or zarrad. Nails should be neither too thin, lest they split, nor too thick, lest they break the rings.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r8.anchor: أي عدل في نسج الدروع ومنه

TABRISI:34:11-12/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r9.speaker: لقمان
TABRISI:34:11-12/r9.claim: Luqman watched David make his first coat in silence, then praised it as excellent war protection; he remarked that silence is wisdom, though few practice it.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r9.anchor: حكي أن لقمان حضر داود عند أول درع عملها فجعل يتفكر فيها

TABRISI:34:11-12/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-12/r10.claim: God told David and his household to perform righteous acts as thanks for His great blessings.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r10.anchor: أي وقلنا اعمل أنت وأهلك الصالحات وهي الطاعات شكرا لله سبحانه على عظيم نعمه

TABRISI:34:11-12/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:34:11-12/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:34:11-12/r11.claim: God knows what they do; none of their deeds is hidden from Him.
TABRISI:34:11-12/r11.anchor: أي أنا عالم بما تفعلونه لا يخفى علي شيء من أعمالكم

FARRA:v2p355#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p355#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p355#2/r2.claim: سابغات refers to coats of mail.
FARRA:v2p355#2/r2.anchor: وقوله- عز وجل- أن أعمل سابغات [11] الدروع

FARRA:v2p355#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p355#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p355#2/r3.claim: The armor’s rivets should be neither so thin that they rattle loose nor so thick that they break the rings.
FARRA:v2p355#2/r3.anchor: (وقدر في السرد) يقول: لا تجعل مسمار الدرع دقيقا فيقلق، ولا غليظا فيقصم الحلق.

THALABI:v8p72/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p72/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p72/r3.claim: A report says David sought a livelihood independent of the treasury after an angel disguised as a man criticized his use of public funds; God softened iron, taught him armor-making, and David sold each suit for four thousand, supporting his family and giving to the poor.
THALABI:v8p72/r3.anchor: وكان سبب ذلك على ما روي في الأخبار أن داود (عليه السلام) لما ملك بني إسرائيل

THALABI:v8p72/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p72/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p72/r5.claim: Sabighat are complete, ample suits of armor.
THALABI:v8p72/r5.anchor: أن اعمل سابغات دروعا كوامل واسعات

THALABI:v8p72/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p72/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p72/r6.claim: Make the rivets neither so thin that links close up nor so thick that they break the rings; David was first to make linked armor, whereas armor had previously been plates.
THALABI:v8p72/r6.anchor: أي لا تجعل المسامير دقاقا فتغلق ولا غلاظا فتكسر الحلق. فكان يفعل ذلك: وهو أول من اتخذ الدروع، وكانت قبل ذلك صفائح،

THALABI:v8p72/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p72/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p72/r7.claim: Sard is armor-making; the maker is called sarād or zarād, and linked armor is musarūd. Abu Dhuʾayb's verse uses musarūdatān for armor David or Tubbaʿ made.
THALABI:v8p72/r7.anchor: والسرد: صنعة الدرع، ومنه قيل لصانعها: السراد والزراد والدرع المسرودة،

THALABI:v8p72/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
