THALABI:v8p72/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p72/r8.claim: The root means joining and ordering; it is also used of beads, an awl, and sequenced speech, as al-Shammakh's verse illustrates for threading reins.
THALABI:v8p72/r8.anchor: وأصله الوصل والنظم، ومنه قيل للخرز: سرد وللأشفى مسرد وسراد.

THALABI:v8p73/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p73/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p73/r1.claim: Sard also describes the ordering or sequencing of speech.

THALABI:v8p73/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p73/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p73/r2.claim: The command to do righteous deeds addresses David and his family; God sees what they do.
THALABI:v8p73/r2.anchor: واعملوا يعني داود وآله صالحا إني بما تعملون بصير

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r1.claim: Sābighāt are broad or ample coats of mail.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r2.claim: Qaddir fī al-sard means to regulate the mail's weaving and rivets: rivets must not be so thin that rings loosen or so thick that they break.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r2.anchor: وقدر في السرد} أي في النسج، أي لا تجعل المسامير دقاقا فتقلق ولا غلاظا فتكسر الحلق.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r3.claim: A maker of mail rings is called sarad or zarad, with s and z alternating as in sirāṭ and zirāṭ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r3.anchor: ومنه قيل لصانع [حلق] الدروع: سراد وزراد. تبدل من السين الزاي، كما يقال: سراط وزراط.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r4.claim: Sard also means sewing or stitching; al-Shammākh's poem uses the word in this sense.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r4.anchor: والسرد: الخرز أيضا. قال الشماخ: كما تابعت سرد العنان الخوازر (1)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p353#7/r5.claim: A hearthstone is also called a misrad or sarad.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq treats أن as explanatory: God softened iron so David could make ample coats of mail; an explanatory particle may introduce an imperative, as in “send to him that he rise.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أن اعمل هاهنا في تأويل التفسير، كأنه قيل: وألنا له الحديد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r2.claim: Al-Layth says sabagha describes a coat or anything long enough to reach the ground; it is used of abundant rain and a plentiful blessing too.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r2.anchor: قال الليث: سبغت الدرع، وكل شيء طال إلى الأرض فهو سابغ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r3.speaker: الهذلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r3.claim: A Hudhalī poet’s phrase al-sawābigh witnesses the use of the word for ample coats of mail.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r3.anchor: ومنه قول الهذلي (¬5): أو صنع السوابغ تبع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Zubayr’s verse describes a sabigha coat covering the fingers like a pool of clear water.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن الزبير: وسابغة تغشى البنان كأنها ... أضاة بضحضاح من الماء ظاهر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq says sabighāt omits the described noun, coats of mail, because the adjective makes that noun understood; a sabigh garment covers what lies beneath and extends beyond it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (ومعنى سابغات: أي: دروع سابغات، فذكر الصفة؛ لأنها تدل على الموصوف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the sabighāt as iron coats of mail.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: في قوله: {أن اعمل سابغات} يريد: دروع الحديد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r7.claim: Muqātil says these were long coats of mail; before David, armor was made of hammered iron plates.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p325/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني: الدروع الطوال، وكانت الدروع قبل داود إنما هي صفائح الحديد مضروبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses it as in the making or links of the armor, and calls a coat dirʿ masrūda; Abū Dhuʾayb’s verse uses masrūdatān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: (في سردها، يقال: درع مسرودة. وقال أبو ذؤيب: وعليهما مسرودتان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r2.claim: Al-Layth says sard is a collective name for coats of mail and similar craftwork, called so because the ends of links are pierced and joined with nails.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r2.anchor: وقال الليث: (السرد: اسم جامع للدروع وما أشبهها من عمل الخلق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses sard as the joining or weaving of armor; the armor-maker is called a sarrād or zarrād, with sīn alternating with zāy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r4.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad says sard is the fastening of nails, and a masrūda coat is armor whose nails have been secured well; al-Aʿshā’s verse attests the term.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r4.anchor: وقال المبرد: السرد نقب المسامير، يقال: درع مسرودة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines sard as arranging things successively so each trace follows the last; the same root describes continuous speech and fasting, three consecutive sacred months, and a row of connected fastenings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: (السرد في اللغة: مقدمة شيء إلى شيء حتى ينسق أثره في أثر بعض سابغا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r6.claim: In Mujāhid’s transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās says not to make nails thin and rings wide so the armor loosens, or nails thick and rings narrow so they break; make them proportionate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية مجاهد: لا تدق المسامير وتوسع الحلق فيسلس، ولا يغلظ المسامير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says sard means the nails in the mail links; the author says this best fits the interpretation shared by all exegetes, who discuss sizing the nails to avoid looseness or breakage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r7.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: السرد: المسامير التي في حلق الدرع (¬4). وهذا هو الأشبه بالمعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r8.claim: Muqātil says to size the nails for the links: oversized nails split them, while undersized ones slip loose.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يقول قدر المسامير في الحلق، ولا تعظمه فينفصم، ولا تصغره فيسلس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r9.claim: Abū Isḥāq says not to pair a thick nail with a narrow hole or a thin nail with a wide hole; make the construction balanced and suited to its need.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r9.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (وهو أن لا يجعل المسمار غليظا والثقب دقيقا، ولا يجعل المسمار دقيقا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r10.speaker: مقاتل وابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r10.claim: Muqātil says God then commands David’s household to act righteously; Ibn ʿAbbās glosses this as thanking God as He deserves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p326/r10.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬8): ثم قال الله لآل داود: {واعملوا صالحا إني بما تعملون بصير} قال ابن عباس: يريدوا اشكروا الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r1.claim: Sābighāt are complete coats of mail.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r1.anchor: دروعا كوامل { وقدر في السرد } لا تجعل مسمار الدرع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r2.claim: Sard is the weaving of chain mail; each rivet should be sized so it neither splits when too thin nor breaks the rings when too thick.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r2.anchor: لا تجعل مسمار الدرع دقيقا فيفلق، ولا غليظا فيفصم الحلق. اجعله على قدر الحاجة، والسرد: نسج الدروع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r3.claim: The command to do good is addressed to David and his family and means doing righteous acts in obedience to God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:34:11-12/r3.anchor: يعني: داود وآله { صالحا } عملا صالحا من طاعة الله تعالى

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r7.claim: The complete, ample garments are coats of armor.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r8.claim: Mujahid says to balance the rivets and rings: undersized rivets with oversized rings make the mail loose, while oversized rivets with undersized rings split the ring.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r8.anchor: تفسير مجاهد: لا تصغر المسمار، وتعظم الحلقة فيسلس

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r9.claim: A report says Luqman watched David make his first coat of mail, wondered about its purpose without asking, then saw David wear it; Luqman called silence wisdom practiced by few.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p747#2/r9.anchor: وبلغنا أن لقمان حضر داود عند أول درع عملها

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r13.claim: The parallel in 21:80 says armor-making protects people from battle; its address to you is directed to Muhammad’s community, suggesting the craft was passed on.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r13.anchor: buyurulmuştu ki bundan bu sanatın ahlâfa da yâdigâr kaldığı anlaşılıyor.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r14.claim: David is told to make ample, full armor and measure its interlinking and form carefully, applying skill to its design.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r14.anchor: ve serdinde takdir sahibi ol yani

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r15.claim: The wisdom in praising armor is that it protects human life from killing; makers of defensive protection benefit humanity more than makers of attack weapons and serve peace.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r15.anchor: bu sanatta لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ buyurulduğu üzere indallah mükerrem olan âdemiyeti katilden muhafaza ile rûhu vikāye vardır.

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r16.claim: Some take the plural command as addressed to David and his household; Elmalılı instead prefers it as an appended lesson addressing Muhammad’s community, as in 21:80.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r16.anchor: bu cümle zamirinin Dâvûd ile beraber maiyyetindeki ehline râci‘olduğunu söylemişler ise de biz bunun لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ gibi kıssanın bir ibreti olmak üzere ümmet-i Muhammed’e hitap ile bir tezyil olduğu kanaatindeyiz

ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r17.claim: God sees whatever people do and will reward them accordingly.
ELMALILI:34:10-11#2/r17.anchor: çünkü ben ne yapacağınızı gözetiyorum, her ne yaparsanız görürüm yani ona göre mükâfâtını veririm.

MAJAZ:v2p143/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p143/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p143/r3.claim: Sābighāt are broad, long coats of mail.
MAJAZ:v2p143/r3.anchor: «أن اعمل سابغات» (11) أي دروعا واسعة طويلة

MAJAZ:v2p143/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p143/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p143/r4.claim: A masrūd coat is mail whose rings are riveted; Abu Dhuʾayb’s verse uses masrūdatān for two such coats.
MAJAZ:v2p143/r4.anchor: «وقدر في السرد» (11) يقال: درع مسرودة أي مسمورة الحلق، قال أبو ذؤيب:

MAJAZ:v2p143/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p143/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p143/r5.claim: Sard is like a ship’s fastening, made with coir or palm fiber; dasarahu with a spear means ‘he stabbed him.’
MAJAZ:v2p143/r5.anchor: مثل دسار السفينة وهو ما خرز به من كنبار أو ليف. ويقال:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r1.claim: David was commanded and specially enabled to make shirt-shaped armor; armor had previously been made from plates.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r1.anchor: Hz. Dâvûd’a gömlek şeklinde zırhlar imal etmesi buyurulmuş ve bunu yapabilmesi için kendisine özel bir yetenek verilmişti; daha önce zırhlar, levha biçiminde yapılırdı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r2.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r2.claim: Ordering finely woven defensive armor rather than an offensive weapon highlights human worth and the importance of protecting life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r2.anchor: Hz. Dâvûd’a ince örgülü zırh gömlek yani taarruz silâhı değil savunma aracı yapmanın emredilmesi ve kendisine bu konuda özel bir beceri verilmesi oldukça mânidardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r3.claim: Another verse explains that armor-making was taught to protect people from other people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r3.anchor: Zaten başka bir âyette zırh yapmayı öğretme insanın yine insana karşı korunması gerekçesiyle açıklanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r4.claim: The shirt form, unlike restrictive plate armor, can also be connected to valuing human beings and their movement.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r4.anchor: İçinde zor hareket edilen levha zırhlar yerine insanın vücuduna uygun gömlek şeklinde zırhlar imalinin istenmesini de insana değer verme temasıyla ilintilendirmek mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r5.claim: The command encourages attention to the details of useful work, continual improvement, and progress in civilization.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r5.anchor: yararlı her işin inceliklerine inmesi, sürekli gelişme içinde olması, böylece uygarlık yolunda mesafe alması yönünde insana yapılmış bir teşvik bulunduğu açıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r6.speaker: Taberî; İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r6.claim: The instruction is commonly explained as spacing interlocking rings carefully: holes must not be too wide to protect or so small and dense that they weaken the armor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r7.claim: Although other readings exist, the wording and context suggest care in the armor's weave, so the author prefers ‘make its weave measured.’
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r7.anchor: âyetin gerek lafzı gerekse bağlamı zırhın örgüsüne özen gösterilmesi anlamını düşündürdüğü için meâlde yukarıda belirtilen mânayı tercih ettik

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r8.speaker: Zemahşerî; İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r8.claim: A story says David disguised himself to ask people's views; an angel in human form praised his rule but faulted his reliance on the treasury, after which David prayed for an independent livelihood and God taught him ironworking.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r9.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r9.claim: The Prophet said the best food is what one earns by one's own labor and that David ate from his own handiwork; the author sees this as explaining the story.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:34:11/r9.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in Dâvûd ile ilgili şu övücü ifadelerinin açıklaması olarak düşünmek uygun olur: “İnsanın yediğinin en güzeli, kendi kazandığıdır. Allah’ın peygamberi Dâvûd da kendi el emeğini yerdi”

NAHHAS:v3p333/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r13.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p333/r13.claim: Abu Ishaq offers two parses: أن explains the command We said to him, or is accusative and links the command to God's softening the iron.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r13.anchor: لأبي إسحاق فيه جوابان أحدهما أن تكون أن بمعنى أي مفسرة تؤدي عن معنى قلنا له اعمل

NAHHAS:v3p333/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p333/r14.claim: سابغات is accusative, with an adjective standing for its noun: complete coats of mail. War armor is feminine, while a woman's coat of mail is masculine.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r14.anchor: ( سائغات ) في موضع نصب وأقيمت الصفة مقام الموصوف أي اعمل دروعا سابغات

NAHHAS:v3p333/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p333/r15.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v3p333/r15.claim: Mujahid says to size each nail so it is neither too thin to slip nor too thick to split the armor.
NAHHAS:v3p333/r15.anchor: قال ابن عيينة عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قدر المسمار لا يكون دقيقا فيسلس ولا غليظا فيفصمها

BURHAN:v3p154/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p154/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p154/r9.claim: سابغات means coats of armor that cover fully.
BURHAN:v3p154/r9.anchor: وقوله ﴿ أن اعمل سابغات ﴾ 7 أي دروعا سابغات

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r1.claim: David and Solomon received a kingdom, knowledge, wisdom, and many blessings without becoming arrogant; they remained grateful and obedient, so God continued increasing His favors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r1.anchor: They never became arrogant and rebellious after receiving these favours; in fact, they continued to remain thankful and obedient to God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r3.claim: The examples confront affluent, arrogant Quraysh with a choice: follow David and Solomon to merit favor, or follow Sheba and incur God's wrath.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r3.anchor: Both these examples are presented before the affluent and arrogant among the Quraysh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r4.claim: Since divine reward and punishment already operate in this world, the examples challenge people to explain why they consider them improbable in the next.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p274/r4.anchor: if God’s law of reward and punishment comes into play in this world, why do they consider it to be improbable in the next world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r6.claim: Sābighāt describes loose-fitting attire covering the whole body, here loose-fitting coats of mail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r6.anchor: The word اتَغِابَس is used for a loose-fitted attire that covers the whole body.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r7.claim: Ṣard means the make or construction of something, while taqdīr means keeping its proportions in view.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r7.anchor: means to keep proportion in consideration while making something.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r8.claim: Making proportioned, loose-fitted iron mail required God to reveal iron-smelting knowledge to David, whose invention advanced defensive weaponry.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p276/r8.anchor: He was the one who originated this technological advancement. With this invention he made a grand contribution to defence weaponry.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r1.claim: The command to do righteous work sets the moral limit for scientific progress: David must not misuse the gift to spread disorder and must remember God watches his deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r1.anchor: the moral right of this advancement is delineated: he should not go astray after being bestowed with this blessing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r2.claim: The warning applies to David, his family, and followers; Islahi says the Psalms and Proverbs repeat it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r2.anchor: This directive is given by God to David (sws) and all his family and followers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r3.claim: Scientific inventions depend on God’s guidance, and every gift or capacity is a trust whose use God observes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r3.anchor: every invention of science owes itself to God’s guidance. Second, it is the natural requirement of every favour and capability that they be regarded a trust from God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r4.claim: When people ignore God’s guidance and their accountability for using gifts, science becomes dangerous; humanity may be destroyed by its own weapons.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p277/r4.anchor: By ignoring both these things, science has become a great danger for man. One cannot say when man may commit suicide from a weapon he has invented himself.

ITQAN:v3p166/r8.speaker: author

ITQAN:v3p166/r8.anchor: حذف الموصوف ﴿ وعندهم قاصرات الطرف ﴾ أي حور قاصرات
